analysis.title: GS MORNING 1) Brazil FX & Rates Update, 2) Brazil Webcast Takeaways, 3) Tony P's Latest and 4) 5 Key Charts Overnight 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: Brazil FX: GS FX strategy expects most of the initial BRL move (~10%) to have occurred already after the first-round election result. Further appreciation depends on policy implementation, cabinet appointments and fiscal measures. A reversal is possible if fiscal measures are not delivered.

The 2018 election is the closest parallel for BRL, with a move of close to 10% over a similar window. Governability looks better for Flavio given the new Congress composition, but fiscal concerns are more pressing than in 2018.

GS FX strategy sees second-round vol falling substantially while longer-dated vol rises, because cabinet appointments (finance ministry) and the 2027 budget due by year end will generate policy-led noise.

Brazil rates: DIs closed about 125bps tighter with a flattening bias and the long end outperforming. The long end hit limit-down twice, with the curve about 150bps tighter at one point. Long-end FRAs are around 12.50, and breaking below 11.5-12% would need a Flavio win plus a credible fiscal package or transition bill.
Brazil flows: net receivers in large size in the long end, with some profit-taking that was small relative to the receiver community.
Brazil webcast: Alberto Ramos expects a gradual multi-year fiscal adjustment under Flavio rather than a front-loaded one, and says political capital must be used quickly.

Brazil webcast: Carlos Loureiro expects EWZ to trade in a 45-50 range for the next few days and sees upside room given P/E ratios and technicals, citing an unprecedented alignment across Congress, Senate and Executive.

Brazil webcast: Thiago Marinheiro says rates have not been very supportive of a rally. After the initial reset, Brazil rates will likely trade more in line with external markets, and a more sustainable rally would need relief in the external market.

Tony Pasquariello says the primary trend remains higher and the tactical setup is net positive, citing strong nominal GDP growth, strong earnings growth, supportive flow of funds and the continuing investment super cycle. He expects Q4 to be choppy but the S&P to be higher on Dec 31 than today.

Pasquariello: higher rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball. The S&P P/E has fallen from 23x to 19x over the past year, rate-sensitive groups (small cap, homebuilders, utilities, REITs, biotech, non-profitable tech) show the impact, and the spread of rates versus the S&P earnings yield has been steady.

Pasquariello says the market is aware that the rate strip prices one more hike this year and about two more next year, and expects stocks to tolerate that. He keeps the view that core length in risky assets should be paired with a trading short in US fixed income.
Pasquariello: consensus expects S&P Q3 EPS growth of 27%. Tech and energy are expected to drive 80% of growth, AI infrastructure half, and NVDA and MU alone about one third.
Pasquariello: NDX is +23% YTD, AI remains the clearest theme, and he expects more air pockets and volatility. US mega cap tech is described as both the sword and the shield.

Key charts: GS estimates the rate rise since Feb 27 will cut 2027 US GDP growth by 0.2pp, leaving growth close to the 2.3% potential estimate. Mortgage rates are up more than 1pp since February, with over 90% of borrowers holding rates below current market levels.
Key charts: global AI investment reaching $1tn in 2026 is estimated to add 0.05pp-0.15pp to 2026 European GDP growth. The PC2 monetary policy factor is at one of its lowest levels since 2000.
Key charts: the S&P 500 is 2% from its ATH while the median stock is 17% below its ATH, leaving market breadth at its lowest since the dot-com bubble.
